body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Friday, October 9, and the top story is a shooting in southwest Bakersfield that sent two people to the hospital and drew a heavy police and fire response to a Pembroke Avenue block just after 1 a.m. Expect a hot one — a high near 97 under clear skies, air quality in the moderate range, and no active weather alerts or fires in Kern County. Here's what happened while you slept.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's biggest call came just after 1:20 a.m., when officers and firefighters were sent to a residence in the 5400 block of Pembroke Avenue in southwest Bakersfield for a report of a shooting. Crews arrived to find two patients with gunshot wounds and quickly set up a perimeter around the block, holding family members back while units moved in. Hall Ambulance staged to enter from the east, and officers asked firefighters to light up the roof to check it for evidence. The scene was secured and turned over to investigators, and the department had not released any details on the victims' conditions by morning.

Deputies in the same hour worked a knife attack on the 1500 block of Lincoln Street. Callers reported a man chasing a woman down the street and attacking others, and radio traffic indicated his mother was threatened with the knife and a sister stepped in front of it. Deputies found the suspect in a cluttered shed area at the back corner of the property and were still sorting out who was hurt. A separate 911 call from nearby reported only a verbal disturbance, and the woman on that call denied anything on the callback.

Elsewhere, officers picked up a newer white Honda Accord reported stolen and moved to stop it near College Avenue and Flint Ridge. About four people bailed out and ran into an open garage, which was then pulled shut, and officers ringed the block in case the car started moving again. One man was described running southbound in a gray shirt, black shorts and a face covering toward Culver and Pioneer. A second stolen-vehicle report — another white Honda Accord, seen near Niles Road and McCurdy Drive — came in the same night. Officers also responded to the Food Maxx on Niles Street for a man with a knife, and a negotiator opened a line with him, calling for him to put the weapon down. The man was described as white, in his late thirties, dressed in black and carrying a pocket knife. Units were moved in from Lamont to cover the area while the call was worked. Earlier in the evening, deputies in the Frazier Park area handled a strong-arm robbery at a travel stop on Taft Highway. The rest of the night was alarms, crashes, disturbances and medical aids — the ordinary hum that keeps deputies busy between the calls that make the report.

## Today's weather

It's currently 73 degrees at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 97 this afternoon — a proper October scorcher, so plan your outdoor work for the morning and keep the water handy. Tonight's low settles around 66. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and no active fires reported in the county. Air quality sits at 76 on the index, which is moderate — fine for most of us, but if you're sensitive to smoke or dust, take it easy during the hottest hours. If you're headed over the Grapevine or down the I-5 corridor, note that all lanes are impacted near Smokey Bear Road south of us due to a fire, with evacuation warnings issued in that area — worth checking conditions before you go.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports a heavy Kern County Sheriff's Office presence in northwest Bakersfield on Friday.** Deputies were out in force in the northwest part of town, though the station's report did not detail the nature of the activity. If you live or drive through that part of the city, expect to see patrol units and give them room to work. We'll pass along more specifics as they become available.

**According to KGET 17, there's no mail on Monday, as the U.S. Postal Service observes a federal holiday.** Post offices will be closed and there will be no regular residential or business delivery that day. If you've got something that absolutely has to go out, get it to the counter or the blue box before the weekend ends — and if you're waiting on a package, add a day to your expectations. It's a good reminder to plan around the holiday rather than be surprised by an empty mailbox.

**Bakersfield Now reports that all lanes of Interstate 5 are impacted near Smokey Bear Road because of a fire, with evacuation warnings issued.** That's the stretch south of us in the Grapevine corridor, a route plenty of Kern County drivers use to get to and from Southern California. If your Friday or weekend plans take you that way, check conditions before you leave and be ready to reroute. Evacuation warnings are not orders, but they mean officials want people in the area ready to move if things change.

**23ABC reports that Kern County voters will decide in November whether a small sales tax increase should fund CALM Zoo's expansion.** Measure Z calls for an increase of one-eighth of a percent countywide — a penny for every $8 spent — with the money going toward the zoo's long-term master plan: expanded animal habitats, new exhibits and improvements to existing facilities. Jim Damian, chair of Yes on Measure Z, told the station that CALM is a treasured community asset that draws roughly 100,000 visitors a year and called the tax an investment worth making. Kern County Republican Mark Bigger opposes it, arguing that Measure Z imposes a permanent tax increase to fund what he calls a nonessential government service, and that families already struggling with rising costs deserve fiscal responsibility instead. The measure's fate now rests with voters in the general election.

**23ABC also reports that the Arvin City Council authorized $26,000 to hire a professional firm to educate voters about Measure H, a proposed one-cent sales tax increase.** The firm, William Berry Campaigns, was brought on in June to educate voters and rally support, and the city has posted information on its website under "Tax Measure H" in the Quick Links. Mayor Olivia Calderon has warned that rejecting the measure could bring deeper cuts, saying the city's reserves were less than $300,000. The council's decision drew backlash on social media over both the message and the price tag, and Council Member Susana Reyes said the outreach portion will be addressed at Tuesday's council meeting. It's a reminder that in a tight budget year, even the cost of making the case for a tax is itself a public expense.

**23ABC reports that Congressman David Valadao picked up dual endorsements Thursday from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the Kern County Farm Bureau.** The endorsements came at a press conference at a plastic manufacturing plant in southeast Bakersfield. Farm Bureau president Todd Snyder cited Valadao's support for Kern agriculture and water; Jennings Imel of the U.S. Chamber pointed to his stances on tax policy, permitting reform and workforce development. Valadao said he plans to keep working across party lines if re-elected, while noting it's unclear whether major federal tax reform will move soon, and that he's focused on the regulatory side of daily costs. For a county whose economy runs on farming and water, the Farm Bureau's nod carries real weight.

**KGET 17 reports that Los Angeles-owned bio-waste farmland continues to impact the Bakersfield community.** The station's report examines the ongoing effects of that land use on residents here. We'll follow the story as it develops.

## Something good

Bakersfield is on track to record its fewest shootings and shooting deaths in years, city officials say — a milestone worth pausing on. Fewer triggers pulled and fewer families shattered is the kind of progress that doesn't always make headlines, but it changes lives block by block. Credit goes to the officers, outreach workers and neighbors doing the quiet, unglamorous work of keeping the peace. Let's hope the trend holds.

## Coming up this week

The week ahead is full of chances to weigh in on city business. Today at noon, two committees meet at City Hall: the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee and the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee — both open to the public, and both good places to hear what's happening on the ground in your neighborhood. Monday brings a doubleheader: the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets at noon, followed by the Fire Civil Service Commission at 3 p.m. Tuesday at noon, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee takes up the city's street and safety priorities — a good one for anyone with opinions about traffic on your commute. Wednesday at 10 a.m., the Water Board meets, and given how much of Kern's economy and daily life runs on water, that's always worth watching. The Planning Commission meets Thursday at 5:30 p.m. to consider land-use and development items. On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater hosts NB RIDAZ: Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off tonight, FANTASIAS on Saturday, United We Dance on October 16, the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour on October 17, and Fortune Feimster's Taking Care of Biscuits tour on October 18. And if you're already thinking ahead to next summer, the Cults & Classics season pass for 2026–2027 is on sale now. Have a good Friday, Bakersfield — stay cool out there.

top.title: Heavy KCSO presence seen in NW Bakersfield Friday
